rss.title: If in doubt, delete the uv.lock file
rss.summary: I've been getting the occasional confusing Python dependency error since switching over to Python 3.15 and the rule I'm having to remember is: If in doubt, delete the uv.lock file Most of my projects are libraries which don't include a uv.lock file, since it's rude for a library dependency to lock versions for anything else that uses it. Running uv run pytest etc tends to leave uv.lock files lying around, which are listed in .gitignore and so do not get committed to my repositories. But... sometimes that uv.lock pins a version of a dependency that doesn't yet have a Python 3.15 wheel. An example from earlier today: error: Failed to build `watchfiles==1.1.1` cause: Call to `maturin.build_wheel` failed error: the configured Python interpreter version (3.15) is newer than PyO3's maximum supported version (3.14) Deleting that file and running uv run pytest again usually fixes the problem. rss.title: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts
rss.summary: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts Parameter Labs describe an exploit they found against ChatGPT's implementation of the artifacts pattern (OpenAI used to call this "Canvas" but it looks like the latest revision is called HTML previews ), where interactive custom HTML apps are displayed in a sandboxed iframe. It's important that HTML in these stays tightly sandboxed to avoid untrusted code interacting with OpenAI APIs and accessing private data. Parameter found quite a complex attack chain. OpenAI use the MathLive JavaScript library as part of their graph support, and that library includes its own virtual keyboard , which can be triggered in the parent page via postMessage() from the sandboxed iframe. That message receiving code uses innerHTML , so anything that sends a message can add custom HTML to the parent - and there was no mechanism to prevent other sandboxed frames, including HTML preview frames, from calling that method. This meant untrusted code in an iframe could insert HTML, and while innerHTML doesn't directly execute script elements it could be used to inject a new iframe without sandbox restrictions. OpenAI’s CSP rules blocked inline scripts entirely, and only allowed script loading from a handful of domains, but one of those was YouTube - and the YouTube oEmbed endpoint could be used to reflect JavaScript back in a way that executed it. Once the attack had JavaScript execution on ChatGPT, it was trivial to fetch private user data from APIs and exfiltrate it via an image reference. The end result: you could create a ChatGPT share URL which, when visited by another signed-in user, could exfiltrate their private data or take actions on their behalf. OpenAI closed the hole and paid out a $5,000 bug bounty, which I think was a bit cheap for a vulnerability this serious. Via Hacker News Tags: iframes , javascript , sandboxing , security , xss , openai , chatgpt , content-security-policy

rss.title: Agents Prompt People: Using Agents for Long-Horizon Financial Work
rss.summary: Arca's head of AI discusses persistent memory, the benefits of a custom harness, and agentic workflows that span days.
rss.text_excerpt:
Arca's head of AI discusses persistent memory, the benefits of a custom harness, and agentic workflows that span days. We discovered that while agents do most of the background work in the firm, there are guardrails in place to ensure that human advisors are making the final decisions. The goal is for AI to guide the process; or as Singh nicely put it, “agents prompt people more than people prompt agents.” Arca recently raised $48.5 Million in a round led by General Catalyst, with participation from Index Ventures and Venrock. One of the features of using AI in financial services, explained Singh, is that it’s typically long-horizon work — although not long-running. In his AIE presentation, Singh noted that agent tasks at Arca can take up to ten days. “It's very stop-start, there's many actors in between, many decision points, many handoffs,” he said. For this reason, Arca has developed an internal memory system . “So we have this persistence for every client ,” Singh said in our podcast discussion. “What has happened so far? What are we tracking for next? What needs to happen immediately in the next couple of days [and] what are we tracking for the long term? Which individual is responsible for which action? All of this is being tracked by our memory systems that our agents contribute to.” Arca uses models from frontier labs like Anthropic and OpenAI, with Claude its primary model provider. The company has built its own harness , which automatically selects the best model to use for a particular task, based on the company’s internal benchmarks. Owning the harness, rather than using a managed agent harness, also means that Arca has the flexibility to change model providers if it needs to. Safety is obviously key for financial services. Singh noted that although agents do much of the work, an agent’s role is limited to analysis and proposing solutions. Trading and any other money movement is handled by a human advisor. “All of our safety restrictions are fully deterministic,” he said. “And they take the decision making off the agent's hands.” In other words, there are certain tools and tasks the agent can execute by itself — but not ones that involve risk to the client. rss.summary: Last week coined the term “Black October“ after an onslaught of critical vulnerability disclosures, including PHP2Shell and a long-standing GitLab bug, signified the moment when the cyber risks of AI models started to materialize.
rss.text_excerpt:
Last week coined the term “ Black October “ after an onslaught of critical vulnerability disclosures, including PHP2Shell and a long-standing GitLab bug, signified the moment when the cyber risks of AI models started to materialize. It seemed like the news cycle had stabilized a bit when I started writing this, but then there was news about another major crypto security incident at Binance . The crypto industry has a very long history of hacks , so it’s not the best industry to indicate vulnerabilities translating into new societal harm. Still, we are very much still living through the implications of this transition. The best guess for what is happening in the cybersecurity space is that the behind the scenes work has only accelerated, bringing more people and resources in to try and patch the internet — the Wall Street Journal reported that cyber first responders are strained , which seems like the system working. We’re living through this plot of an exponential rise in vulnerabilities, which will take a long time to level off at the top of the sigmoid. A few weeks ago, before the rapid acceleration in vulnerability disclosures and the uptick in reported hacks, I wrote the following take. It’s been getting a pretty consistent barrage of feedback, some hopeless dunk attempts and some reasonable discussion, so I wanted to unpack where I stand. Share Open-weight Mythos in April would’ve been fine? When Claude Mythos was announced, it was previewed as if it was a new class of cyber weapon, where if it ended up in the wrong hands it would’ve caused mass societal destabilization. It seems like this was wrong. By all measures, GLM-5.3 is the model that crosses that threshold of capability, and there’s little public evidence that much has changed, and we’re over a month out of the model weight release. rss.title: Making it easier for websites to express AI training preferences
rss.summary: OpenAI will honor a shared robots.txt signal to help website operators communicate their AI training preferences to participating providers.
rss.text_excerpt: Today, we’re announcing that OpenAI will honor a common signal ⁠ (opens in a new window) in robots.txt, the file that lets websites express their preferences about the use of their content for foundational generative AI training. This voluntary effort makes it easier for publishers and website operators to communicate the same preference to multiple participating providers at once. Previously, website operators would identify individual crawlers and maintain separate rules for each and every provider. Having a shared signal across multiple providers reduces that work for operators. We aim to implement the signal in the coming months, and will share another update with details about our implementation when we do so. This new signal will not replace the controls we already provide through robots.txt. Our existing crawler controls ⁠ (opens in a new window) , which provide web publishers flexibility and control over their pages, will continue to apply and be respected. This draws on the ongoing work ⁠ (opens in a new window) of the Internet Engineering Task Force’s (IETF) AI Preferences working group. We’re joining other participants in the working group in today’s announcement of this shared signal, and believe this strengthens our continued participation in the IETF standards discussions. OpenAI will continue to adapt its practices as those conversations and the landscape continue to evolve in view of appropriate controls and fairness. We believe this is a practical step toward an open web where people can publish and discover information, and website owners have clearer, simpler ways to communicate their choices about how their content is used. We encourage other AI providers to honor the signal.

CODE is the last flagship AIE of the year (there are also 2 partner conferences coming up - AIEi Shanghai takes place next week, and AIEi Sydney is a side event of NeurIPS in December). As a Summit it is meant to be more intimate: single track, invite-only for the top 1000 agentic engineers in the world (over 100k tuned into our Software Factories track at WF26 ). My goal in curating AIE CODE is to try to recap the top themes of 2026 in code and gather the leaders of the industry to preview what’s next in 2027. Last year we had some absolute bangers building Skills and Software Factories , predicting the death of the IDE and of course the launch of Antigravity and Nano Banana Pro. We have three themes this year: Scaling without Slop : Last year’s call for No More Slop has resulted in lots of discussions about managing it this year, including the rise and fall of Tokenmaxxing . Our Scaling without Slop approach has mostly worked; we need more. System One models : We believe S1 “smart software” is the largest change to AI Engineering that refreshingly explores the opposite direction to ever larger and more expensive and questionably productive swarms of coding agent FactoryFactoryFactories. While Diogo took pains to explain the difference between Decision Models and System One models on our podcast and his WF26 talk , it has largely been lost to the broader audience. Diogo and team TypeSafe are back for a mini “Jev Day” to show how System One models are truly being used by their top users. # BabyAgent - 后端工程师的 AI Agent 教学项目 (Go 语言版) 🏠 **项目地址：** https://github.com/baby-llm/baby-agent 🚀 **从后端视角出发，用 Go 语言手写一遍 Agent 框架的关键原理。** 本项目专为没有 LLM 背景但具备基础 Golang 经验的后端工程师设计。我们将跳过复杂的数学推导，优先从工程实现理解核心概念：你会看到每一步为什么这么设计、替代方案是什么、以及它们在真实系统里会遇到哪些坑。 > **重要说明（请先读）** > > - 本项目是**教学仓库**：目标是用可运行的代码把 Agent、Tool Calling、Agent Loop、MCP、Memory、RAG 等机制讲清楚。 > - 本项目**不是**“开箱即用的生产框架”，也**不建议直接用于生产环境的二次开发**。 > - 如果你希望落地到真实业务：这里更适合作为**原理参考 + 原型验证**的起点，你需要根据自己的场景补齐工程化能力与安全边界。 --- ## 🏗 核心技术栈 * **Language:** Go 1.25+ * **LLM Concepts:** Chat Completions API, SSE 流式传输, Function Calling, ReAct Agent Loop * **Advanced AI:** 上下文工程, Memory 系统, Agentic RAG, 技能系统（Skills） * **System Design:** MCP 协议, Guardrails 安全防护, Web 服务化 * **Engineering:** LLM 评测, 可观测性（Trace/Metrics/Log） > **SDK fork**：项目通过 `go.mod` 的 `replace` 使用 [baby-llm/openai-go](https://github.com/baby-llm/openai-go)（基于 `openai-go v3.24.0`）。该 fork 在 SDK 层原生支持 `reasoning_content`，避免在业务代码里手工拼装该字段；`go.mod` 中的 `replace` 与 `shared/client.go` 就是全部接入点。 --- ## 🗺 学习路径图 (按知识循序渐进) 我们将按照"从基础调用到复杂 Agent"的顺序逐步深入，带你完成从零到复杂 Agent 的蜕变。每一阶段都包含可运行的代码示例。 ### 第一章：初识 LLM（Raw HTTP 与 OpenAI SDK） **目标**：拨开 SDK 的迷雾，直视大模型调用的本质。 * **协议本质**：掌握 `chat/completions` 接口的最小化请求和响应结构 * **流式输出解析**：深入了解 SSE（Server-Sent Events）协议，实现"打字机"效果 * **工程实践**：对比 Raw HTTP 和 OpenAI Go SDK 的使用方式 * **LLM 原理**（可选）：Transformer、训练过程、Token 机制、生成原理 ### 第二章：赋予 AI "手脚"（Tool Calling 和 Agent） **目标**：让 LLM 从"只会聊天"升级为"能动手做事"的 Agent。 * **Function Calling 协议**：如何向模型声明工具、如何解析工具调用 * **Agent Loop**：工具调用 → 反馈 → 再推理的闭环流程 * **ReAct/Tool-Loop 原理**：Reason + Act 的思维-行动交替模式 * **本地工具封装**：读取文件、写入文件、编辑文件、执行 shell 命令 * **Chat Template**（可选）：从 API 到模型输入的转换机制 ### 第三章：让 Agent "更能看见"（Reasoning 展示、TUI） **目标**：可视化展示推理与工具调用过程，兼容推理模型。 * **推理字段兼容**：解析流式响应中的 `reasoning_content` 字段 * **TUI 可视化**：使用 Bubble Tea 实现轻量的可视化输出 * **流式输出与 UI 协程**：通过 channel 将增量消息传递给 UI * **推理模型 vs 非推理模型**（可选）：Chat Template 差异、Token 消耗特点 ### 第四章：让 Agent 接入 MCP 生态 **目标**：接入 MCP（Model Context Protocol）工具生态，扩展 Agent 能力。 * **MCP 原理**：Client/Server/Tool 三类角色，解决"模型 × 工具"爆炸组合问题 * **协议交互流程**（可选）：JSON-RPC 2.0、初始化、工具发现、工具调用 * **工具管理**：本地工具与 MCP 工具的无缝共存 * **命名空间化**：避免工具冲突的命名策略 ### 第五章：上下文工程（Context Engineering） **目标**：实现完整的上下文管理策略，在有限窗口内高效运行。 * **上下文窗口问题**：理解多轮对话后的窗口限制、成本增加、性能下降 * **截断策略（Truncation）**：安全删除旧消息，保留最近关键对话 * **卸载策略（Offloading）**：将长消息存储到外部，保留恢复提示 * **摘要策略（Summarization）**：使用 LLM 对历史对话进行压缩 * **策略模式设计**：可扩展、可组合的策略接口 * **策略事件系统**：在 TUI 中实时展示策略执行状态 *

github.text_excerpt: # Swarm Map > **Swarm Map (SM)** — formerly Hermes Swarm Map / HSM. A commons, public goods project of [NimbleCo](https://www.nimbleco.ai/). **Multiplayer admin and orchestrator platform for heterogeneous agent runtimes.** One dashboard for two shapes of agent: [Hermes](https://github.com/cyborg-garden/hermes-agent-mt) agents, where each agent is its own container, and [Letta](https://github.com/letta-ai/letta) agents, where memory-first agents live as rows on one shared server. Multi-tenant security, model cascades, and platform connections come from the same control plane either way. *First of its kind, a point and click GUI for not just managing agent runtimes, but also who can do what and where. Solves the multi-tenant agent problem. View the godhead of complexity without derealizing. Share compute.* **Runtime support is not symmetrical yet.** Hermes is the mature path; Letta support is read-only plus send-a-message. See [Runtimes](docs/runtimes.md) for the exact shipped/not-shipped line — we would rather you read a boring matrix than discover the gap after deploying. *Calm UX showing a variety of config settings across agent harness runtimes* --- ## Why Swarm Map? AI agents are most useful when they're always on — running on a server, reachable from your phone, remembering context across conversations. But running *multiple* agents across *multiple* platforms for *multiple* users? That's where it gets hard. Swarm Map is the control plane. One UI to deploy, configure, and manage a fleet of agents — each with its own personality, memory, platform connections, and budget. Everything a single agent can do, but multiplied and multiplayer. It also gets harder when your agents aren't all the same *shape*. A Hermes agent is a container you can start, stop, rebuild, and attach messaging surfaces to. A Letta agent is a row in a shared server's database with a memory-first architecture — no container of its own, nothing to `docker restart`. AI 的每一处修改都以逐字对比交到你面前；默认的「询问」档下，你点头才写进稿子。 [![最新版本](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/XZZKANY/StoryForge?display_name=tag&sort=semver&label=%E6%9C%80%E6%96%B0%E7%89%88%E6%9C%AC&color=4f46e5)](https://github.com/XZZKANY/StoryForge/releases/latest) [![下载量](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/XZZKANY/StoryForge/total?label=%E4%B8%8B%E8%BD%BD%E9%87%8F&color=16a34a)](https://github.com/XZZKANY/StoryForge/releases) [![平台](https://img.shields.io/badge/%E5%B9%B3%E5%8F%B0-Windows%2010%20%2F%2011-0078d4)](#下载安装) [![许可证](https://img.shields.io/github/license/XZZKANY/StoryForge?label=%E8%AE%B8%E5%8F%AF%E8%AF%81&color=0ea5e9)](LICENSE) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/XZZKANY/StoryForge?style=flat&color=f59e0b)](https://github.com/XZZKANY/StoryForge/stargazers) [**下载安装**](#下载安装) · [**三分钟上手**](#三分钟上手) · [**功能一览**](#功能一览) · [**常见问题**](#常见问题) · [**参与开发**](#参与开发) **简体中文** · [English](README.en.md)

截图中的作品《雾港回声》与 AI 回复均为演示内容。

## 为什么做 StoryForge 写长篇，难的往往不是写出一段漂亮的话，而是写到第八十章还记得第三章埋了什么、谁在哪儿、那把钥匙在谁手里。 通用聊天工具看不见你的整部书，每次都要把前情重新贴一遍；一键生成又把作者挤出了创作。StoryForge 走的是第三条路： - **你是作者，AI 是编辑和助手。** 它读稿、挑问题、提改法、起草初稿；正文怎么写，默认由你拍板，「询问」档下每个补丁都要你点接受。 - **整部书随时可查。** Agent 会自己翻目录、读章节、全书检索，并参照大纲和人物设定回答你。 - **改动看得见、撤得回。** 对正文的修改都以补丁出现：逐字对比、写前快照、写后一键撤销。 ## 功能一览 ### 对话式 Agent：一个会自己查全书的编辑 - 直接用中文提要求：「审一下第 5 章的节奏」「第 12 章和第 3 章的设定对得上吗」「起草第 7 章」。 - 要读哪些文件由 Agent 自己决定：列目录、读章节、全书检索，每一步都记在对话里，展开「已思考」就能逐条看。 - 多视角审稿、定向修订、起草新章、跨章一致性检查、深度一致性排查，在同一个对话里完成。 - 说「起草第 7 章」「写下一章」这类话时，先拟章纲，随即写稿、自检，最后以补丁交给你；别的说法可能由 Agent 直接起草，不经章纲。 ### 逐字对比，默认你点头才落盘 - AI 对正文的每一次修改都是一个补丁：可以整体接受、逐块接受、直接拒绝，也可以「拒绝，并告诉 AI 怎么改」让它重来。 - 写入前自动存快照，写入后右下角一键撤销。补丁只改它指出的那几处，你在别处的改动会保留；补丁对应的原文已被你改过，就拒绝写入。 - 权限按作品设置：**只读**（只回答，不改正文；连载计划、canon 缓存等 `.storyforge/` 文件仍可 [TRUNCATED]

# Roam **在手机上继续使用电脑里的 Claude Code / Codex** —— 把电脑端的终端 / 文件 / 屏幕带到任意设备的浏览器上,再加一个跑在云端、能操作你电脑的 AI 助理。 机器不暴露公网。电脑端主动连 Cloudflare Worker,远程网页也只连 Worker。终端、文件、屏幕的数据只经 Worker 中继,不落地;助理的对话和配置存在你自己 Cloudflare 账号的 D1 里。全部用免费额度,不用绑卡。 | 终端 | 文件管理 | 系统状态 | |---|---|---| | ![终端](https://pub-5cb9f2ea49ac433aba4c20d46cd886e7.r2.dev/posts/roam-v2/01-terminal.png) | ![文件管理](https://pub-5cb9f2ea49ac433aba4c20d46cd886e7.r2.dev/posts/roam-v2/02-files.png) | ![系统状态](https://pub-5cb9f2ea49ac433aba4c20d46cd886e7.r2.dev/posts/roam-v2/03-status.png) | 社区讨论: [LINUX DO](https://linux.do) > **顺便打个广告**:我目前主力在做的另一个项目是 [AIOS](https://github.com/valueriver/AIOS) —— 用 AI 直接构建一个操作系统,欢迎去看看、Star、提 issue。 ## 项目组成 ```text roam/ ├─ worker/ # Cloudflare Worker + Vue 前端;Durable Object 负责中继和 AI 助理 ├─ computer/ # 电脑端,提供终端 / 文件 / 屏幕,并执行助理的工具调用 └─ extension/ # Roam 浏览器插件,让助理操作本机 Chrome / Edge ``` 运行时链路: ```text 远程浏览器 ↓ https / wss Cloudflare Worker(终端/文件/屏幕只中继;助理跑在这里,对话存 D1,图片存 R2(可选)) ↓ wss(带 DEVICE_TOKEN) Roam Computer(终端 / 文件 / 屏幕 / 执行助理的工具) ``` ## 能力 - 远程终端 - AI 助理(agent,来自 agentic):模型调用和对话在云端,电脑关机也能翻看历史;要动电脑时把工具调用发给电脑端执行,可执行命令、读写和修改文件、看图、操作浏览器 - 文件浏览、读取、上传、重命名、删除 - 屏幕截图查看 - 固定远程连接 session id ## 前置要求 - Node.js 22+ - Cloudflare 账号,免费计划就行(用到 Workers、Durable Objects、D1;想让助理收发图片再开 R2,开通 R2 要绑卡) - 一台运行 Roam Computer 的电脑 ## 部署 Worker ```bash git clone https://github.com/yanglongyun/roam cd roam/worker npm install cp wrangler.example.jsonc wrangler.jsonc ``` 建好助理要用的数据库: ```bash npx wrangler d1 create roam ``` 编辑 `worker/wrangler.jsonc`: - `account_id`:Cloudflare account id,可用 `npx wrangler whoami` 查看 - `d1_databases[0].database_id`:上一步 `d1 create` 打印的 id - `routes`:可选,自定义域名;不用就删掉整个 `routes` 段 建表、设两个密钥(都用随机串,比如 `openssl rand -base64 32` 生成): ```bash npx wrangler d1 execute roam --remote --file=server/agent/schema.sql npx wrangler secret put SETTINGS_KEY # 加密保存模型 API Key 用,设了别再改 npx wrangler secret put DEVICE_TOKEN # 电脑端接入凭据,下面 config.js 填同一个值 ``` 部署: ```bash npm run deploy ``` 部署完成后得到 Worker 地址,例如: - `https://roam.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev` - `https://i.example.com` ### 可选:开启图片(R2) 不开 R2 时,助理只能收发文字:网页上不显示发图按钮,`read` 读图片、`browser` 截图也看不到图片内容(浏览器工具改用读网页文字和元素位置)。 要开的话,先在 Cloudflare 控制台开通 R2(需要绑卡,免费额度每月 10 GB),然后: ```bash npx wrangler r2 bucket create roam ``` 把 `worker/wrangler.jsonc` 里 `r2_buckets` 段的注释去掉,再 `npm run deploy`。 ## 配置 Computer ```bash cd ../computer npm install cp config.example.js config.js

# skein-js [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/skein-js?logo=npm&color=cb3837&label=skein-js)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/skein-js) [![downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/skein-js?color=blue)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/skein-js) [![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/skein-js?color=green)](./LICENSE) [![CI](https://github.com/skein-js/skein-js/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/skein-js/skein-js/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-skein--js.github.io-3b82f6)](https://skein-js.github.io/skein-js/) **Run LangGraph.js agents on your own infrastructure.** skein-js is an open-source TypeScript runtime for hosting [LangGraph.js](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/javascript/langgraph/overview) agents. LangGraph defines and executes your graphs; Skein provides the API, persistence, streaming, background work, and console around them. ## Why skein-js? A graph that works in a script still needs a backend before people can use it. Conversations need state, long-running work needs a queue, and people need a way to see what happened or approve the next step. Building and maintaining that infrastructure takes time away from your application. Skein supplies that backend. Keep your graph code, models, and tools, then run it as a service on your infrastructure or inside an application you already ship. It is an Apache-2.0 alternative to LangGraph Platform (now LangSmith Deployment), with no commercial license key required. Build a customer-facing assistant, a research tool, or a workflow that waits for human approval. Your existing LangGraph SDK clients and Agent Chat UI connect through the same Agent Protocol: the HTTP and streaming API around your graphs. ## What you get - **Conversation state and long-term memory.** Keep conversation history and recall information across threads. Use Postgres for shared servers or SQLite for local persistence.
